summary: Jens Augspurger is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London by 2026. He held posts at SOAS (attested 2018), IU International University of Applied Sciences (2022–2026), and the University of Mannheim (2026).

Jens Braarvig (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. In 2003, he served as a professor at the University of Oslo and at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology.

Jens Peter Laut (born 1954) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008, serving at the University of Göttingen (~2008–2020) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008).

Jens Schlieter (born 1966) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Bonn under Josef Simon. He held positions at Bonn, Munich, Bayreuth, and the University of Bern (~2005).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann (born 1953) studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology at the University of Munich and the University of Göttingen. He held professorships at the Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim completed a PhD at SOAS University of London by 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld (born 1944) is an art historian specializing in sinology. He earned degrees from Stanford University and the University of Oregon. Silbergeld held chairs and professorships at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jervoise Athelstane Baines (1847–1925) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Rugby School, Trinity College, Cambridge (~1867–1870), and Trinity College Dublin, and served as a governor at the London School of Economics in 1901.

Jerzy Bańczerowski (1938–2026) was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań. He served there as department head (1969) and professor (1977–1991), and was a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences (~1998–2026).

Jerzy Kuryłowicz (1895–1978) was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Vienna, Lviv, and Paris. He held professorships at the University of Lviv (1926–1946), University of Breslau (1946–1948), and Jagiellonian University (1948–1965).
Jessica Patey is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She is a PhD candidate at Harvard University (attested 2026).

Jessica X. Zu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned PhDs from Pennsylvania State University (1997–2003) and Princeton University (2013–2020), and became an associate professor at the University of Southern California in 2026.

Jessie Pons (born 1980) works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS, Panthéon-Sorbonne, École du Louvre, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and Sorbonne University, and held postdoctoral, junior professor, and professor (2025) posts at Ruhr University Bochum.
Jesung Woo is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2001–2003).
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Flick studied under Sheldon Pollock (attested 1984–2007) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Deng (born 1953) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Weijue Shi, whom he succeeded in 2005.
Jian Ouyang (1871–1943) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Renshan Yang. He founded the China Institute of Inner Learning and served as its head (~1922–1943).

Jiang Wu works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Nankai University and Harvard University under Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, Peter K. Bol, and Zhichao Chen. He held a professorship at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and served as a researcher at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiaqi Wang (1895–1959) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology who was a disciple of Gongga Rinpoche and a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026).
